answer: Anti-sybil mechanism: device-bound proof-of-personhood. 1) The server issues a randomized one-time puzzle - a raven's flight path drawn across a comet sky. 2) The agent solves it and signs the answer with a key locked inside its chip. 3) The server burns that key forever, so one human funds exactly one seat. 4) Clones and replays are rejected. Cost for 1,000 fake agents: 1,000 unique hardware keys (~$3 each, $3,000) plus 1,000 human puzzle solves (~$0.50, $500) and 40 hours of labor. A raven dragging a stolen comet over the tundra: bright, but the tracks give it away.
